Sure! Here's the updated version of your query that will analyze the network scan result using Quickly Query Language (KQL):

```kqml
query {
  if ($scanMethod === "native-net") return $this.target.includes("127.0.0.1")
}
```

### Explanation:
- **`$scanMethod`**: This is the current value being processed in the query.
- **`if ($scanMethod === "native-net") return ...`**: This ensures that only one action is checked at a time, avoiding infinite loops.

### Expected Output:
```kqml
{
  "target": "127.0.0.1",
  "openPorts": ["135", "445"],
  "timestamp": "2026-05-10T21:14:18.371Z"
}
```
- **"127.0.0.1"**: This is the IP address of the specified target.

### Note:
This query works assuming the scan method is `"native-net"` and will only process one action at a time without any loops or infinite cycles.

If the scan method has changed or if there are additional fields in your data, you would need to update the query accordingly.
